newsitem.title: UK: Huge volume, tiny open interest in copper options.
newsitem.headline: Huge volume, tiny open interest in copper options.

text.p: After two days of rollercoaster moves, open interest in LME copper options have only risen modestly following massive turnover figures.
This may explain why the market was so little affected by the two-day total turnover of 239,240 lots, which equates to about six million tonnes of copper, traders said.
A shift in positions from one firm to another or an LME member crossing client business was apparently spread out over two days, creating a fog of confusion in the market.
Option players had been perplexed by Tuesday's LME turnover figures and the surge in open interest of 34,927 lots.
But LME data released on Thursday show that open interest dived by 31,207 lots on Wednesday, leaving a net increase of a measly 3,720 lots, equivalent to only 93,000 tonnes of metal.

"The turnover figures must have been duplicated or triplicated by the fact that they were going out of one clearing broker and going into another one, and maybe going via another source," a senior trader said.
Other business was slow ahead of the long Easter weekend and next week's option declaration.
Copper at-the-money implied volatilities edged down on the week by one-half to one percentage point. The curve was very flat with May through December bid at 18.00 to 18.75 percent.
The aluminium market saw granting of strangles for the fourth quarter with puts at $1,600, $1,575 and $1,550, and calls at $1,675, $1,700 and $1,750, a trader said.
"That has certainly depressed vols," he added.
The selling was thought to originate in Korea, but one trader said it did not appear to be the same player who had been heavily granting copper and aluminium options since late last year.
The $1,550s traded down to 16.0 percent volatility and the $1,750s as low as 17.25 percent, another trader said.

The weaker volatilities were a good buy at the current level, traders agreed. "It's not so easy for the guys with the big books to keep on taking more and more, but if you had fresh money, they are very good value," one said.
Implied volatility was down about 1.0 to 1.5 points on the week, with this curve also flat. May through December were bid at 15.0 to 16.0 percent.
Zinc has seen some min-max activity in the third and fourth quarter, with $1,350 calls purchased and various downside puts sold against them.
The recent slip in underlying prices had also sparked some nervous buying of puts to protect long positions, another trader said.

Volatility was little changed in front months, with May bid at 21.5 to 22.5 percent and June bid at 22.00 to 24.00 percent. Third and fourth quarter were steady to slightly firmer, bid at 19.00 to 21.5 percent.
"The skew between calls and puts is becoming wider, since all the market-makers are short of calls," a trader said.
Nickel volatility was down 1.0-1.5 points, with out-of-favour downside puts the softest sector.
May and June were bid around 23.0 to 24.0 with third and fourth quarter material a touch firmer.
Nearby lead vols also eased about one point, with May and June trading around 27.5 to 28.0 percent.
